summary: APIGW 503s during graceful-shutdown race causing ephemeral-worker livelock and runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer traffic burst for BrightLearn (dedicated tenant in us-west), the API gateway returned elevated 503 responses for a ~45 minute window. Concurrently several serving-runtime pods for the tenant entered rapid restart cycles and ephemeral-worker counts grew without successful request completion. The pattern correlated with a rolling node upgrade and a concurrent autoscaler activity.

Impact:
- BrightLearn observed ~40% of requests return 503 for 45 minutes across generative endpoints and embedding uploads.
- Customer reported visible errors in their app and opened an escalation.
- Internal SLO for tenant availability breached.

Environment:
- prod: us-west (dedicated cluster for BrightLearn)
- API Gateway version: apigw-2.14.1
- Serving runtime image: rwinf-1.9.3
- Autoscaler: tenant-autoscaler-v3

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Large upstream traffic spike from BrightLearn (concurrent embedding batches + long-stream chat sessions).
2) Kube node rolling upgrade (control-plane-initiated maintenance) triggers graceful shutdown notifications for some runtime pods.
3) API gateway starts retrying in-flight streams to ephemeral worker pool while shutdown handoff is ongoing.
4) Ephemeral workers accept new streams but cannot complete due to shared GPU scheduling starvation; request token-queues back up and gateway returns 503 when backpressure threshold reached.

Relevant logs / metrics (samples):
- apigw logs: "upstream timeout after retry-loop threshold=3 status=503 tenant=brightlearn"
- runtime logs: "SIGTERM received, entering graceful shutdown, draining connections=0/64" then repeated "worker acquired but scheduling blocked"
- kube events: "PodTermination: preStop hook delayed by 28s; node.cordon: rolling-update"
- metrics: GPU scheduling wait-time spiked from 5ms -> 420ms; ephemeral-worker count climbed 3x; request queue length per-tenant hit configured max 1024.

Investigation timeline and notes:
- 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Support received BrightLearn alert. First response sent (Maya).
- 2026-03-10 10:18 UTC: SRE paged. Initial dashboards show concurrent autoscaler scale-up and node rolling-update.
- 2026-03-10 10:45 UTC: Repro harness simulated similar burst; confirmed gateway retries + pod shutdowns produce same 503 pattern.
- 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC: Engineering identified a shutdown handoff race: runtime sets draining flag but ephemeral-worker admission controller continued to route new streaming sessions.
- 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: apigw rate-limit for tenant reduced and gateway retry-window shortened; this reduced 503 rate.
- 2026-03-10 13:10 UTC: Patch deployed to runtime admission controller to reject new ephemeral sessions when draining=true.

Root cause analysis (summary):
A race between node/pod graceful shutdown flow and the ephemeral-worker admission controller allowed API Gateway to continue routing new sessions to runtime instances that were in transparent draining state. The draining instances still reported capacity to the scheduler (metrics lag) and ephemeral workers accepted session handoffs but could not schedule GPU work due to a transient scheduling window during node drain and concurrent autoscaler activity. The result was a livelock: workers accepted streams but could not progress, queueing requests until API Gateway's backpressure thresholds triggered 503 responses.

Resolution and rollout:
- Hotfix: apigw retry-window shortened + tenant-specific rate cap applied (rolled 10:45-12:30 UTC).
- Code fix: runtime admission controller updated to immediately reject new ephemeral-session handoffs when pod enters draining state (PR: https://github.com/redwood/repro/pull/4321). Deployed canary 12:50 UTC, full rollout 13:10 UTC.
- Post-deploy verification: 503 rate returned to baseline within 20 minutes, GPU scheduling wait-time returned to normal.

Workarounds for customer during incident:
- Recommended BrightLearn to temporarily reduce concurrent embedding batch size and postpone non-critical long-lived streaming sessions until issue resolved. Support provided sample config.

Follow-up actions / action items:
- Engineering: add a metric export for "draining_admission_rejections" and alert when ephemeral-worker acceptance while draining>0 (owner: Evan).
- SRE: update rolling-update runbook to pause autoscaler scaling during node drains for dedicated clusters (owner: Priya Singh).
- Product: communicate post-mortem and recommended tenant configuration for scheduled maintenance windows to Dedicated customers.
- Customer Success: schedule a follow-up with BrightLearn to review incident, credits, and guidance.

Notes on related tickets and investigation artifacts:
- Linked INT-4021 for autoscaler interaction analysis.
- Reproduction PR and test harness in https://github.com/redwood/repro/pull/4321.
- Runbook page created: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Graceful+Shutdown+Race+Runbook

resolution: Hotfix + runtime admission controller change deployed. Reject new ephemeral-session handoffs when pod is draining; apigw retry-window adjusted. Incident resolved and baseline restored.
notes: This incident exposed a coupling between rolling upgrades and autoscaler behavior for dedicated clusters; prioritized follow-up in next reliability sprint.
Recommend a safe-mode flag in autoscaler to suppress scale actions during disruptive maintenance windows for tenant-specific clusters.
